Jasmine — attaching our redline for Exhibit C (pricing schedule). We appreciate the earlier conversation with Ben and Karthik. A few things our counsel flagged that we need clarified and cleaned up before exec approval: 

1) Mid-quarter tier upgrades: the redline changes the proration language to a full-quarter billing model unless explicitly agreed in writing — our concern is exposure to unexpected retainer credits on upgrades. Can you confirm Redwood's position on proration mechanics when a customer moves from Bronze->Silver mid-month?

2) Guardrail floors: we removed the proposed "stability floor" clause; we need assurance that any fee floors won't create double-charges during ramp-downs. How does Redwood handle overlapping true-ups and invoice credits if usage drops under the floor in the same billing period?

3) Carrier packaging credits: we added language preventing tier consolidation from triggering retroactive price increases for bundled SKUs. We need a written example to demonstrate how a consolidated slab would be applied to mixed SKU usage.

4) Cap on temporary surcharges: legal wants an explicit cap and sunset for any temporary surcharges (e.g., marketplace surcharge) — suggest a 3% not-to-exceed and 6-month sunset.

We left inline comments in the attached PDF and a small worksheet that illustrates a few hypothetical month transitions. Can someone from your side respond line-by-line? We need to lock Exhibit C by 10/20 to hit our procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Marta
Marta Ruiz

Nimbio Health

Marta — thanks for the redline and the worksheet. We've reviewed with legal and billing ops; high-level responses below and we'll follow up with an annotated PDF and a worked example by EOD tomorrow. Short answers first: 

1) Proration on mid-cycle upgrades: Redwood's standard behavior is pro-rata credit for unused portion of the prior tier and charge for the remainder at the new tier for the billing period (time-based daily proration). The default is pro-rata unless the order form explicitly elects quarterly billing for upgrades. If Nimbio prefers quarterly bucketing, we can add a checkbox election on the order form.

2) Floors and true-ups: our billing system treats floors as minimum monthly committed spend; if usage falls below the floor we invoice the floor and then apply credits/true-ups on the next billing cycle only. We do not double-charge — the system will not invoice both a floor and a separate true-up for the same consumption; credits are applied against the subsequent invoice. We'll add clarifying language to the clause to avoid ambiguity.

3) Consolidated slab for mixed SKUs: we'll produce a worked example showing mixed SKU aggregation rules (weighting, bundling rules, and whether a SKU can be carved out). Our default is to aggregate usage by billing metric family unless a SKU is explicitly excluded via the packaging annex. We'll propose language that preserves protections against retroactive increases.

4) Temporary surcharge cap: Redwood is amenable to a capped temporary surcharge with sunset; suggest aligning on 3% and 6 months as a compromise. We will mark that in the markup.

Next steps: Ben and Karthik will draft the updated Exhibit C markup and the Excel with worked scenarios. Expect an annotated PDF + worksheet by 2026-10-14 18:00 PDT. If Nimbio needs the quarterly-election checkbox on the order form earlier, let us know and we'll prioritize.

Best,
Jasmine

Marta — attaching the annotated Exhibit C and a worked example spreadsheet per Jasmine's note. Key callouts inline: 

- Section 2(a) (Proration): changed to explicit daily pro-rata model with optional quarterly-election checkbox (redline shows checkbox text). Example on sheet "Upgrade Scenarios" (rows 12-22) illustrates Bronze->Silver upgrade on 2026-10-10 with daily proration and refund credit calculation.

- Section 3(b) (Floor treatment): clarified that floor invoices are applied, and any subsequent true-up credits are posted on the next invoice; removed phrasing that could be read to permit duplicate charges.

- Annex A (SKU bundling): added a "packaging carveout" clause allowing customers to nominate up to 3 SKUs for exclusion from consolidation per year, provided notice 30 days before the next invoice period. This preserves Nimbio's protection while allowing Redwood operational predictability.

- Temporary surcharge cap: added a clause capping temporary surcharges at 3% with a 6-month sunset, and requiring 30 days written notice before activation.

Please review the embedded worksheet and the annotated PDF. If the carveout election is acceptable, we'll add a short checkbox section on the order form so procurement can tick excluded SKUs at signature. If legal prefers the exclusion to be unlimited but narrower in scope, let us know and we'll iterate.

Thanks,
Ben

• The quarterly-election checkbox is fine, but legal insists on an explicit definition of "quarter" (calendar vs. billing cycle). Please define as calendar-quarter for consistency with our financial systems.

• Regarding the SKU carveout (up to 3 SKUs): counsel wants a process paragraph that includes (i) Nimbio provides SKU list 30 days prior to next invoice, (ii) Redwood confirms feasibility within 7 business days, and (iii) any rejected carveouts are escalated to Redwood's commercial lead with a resolution timeline.

• For clarity on the floor/true-up interplay: can Redwood add an illustrative line in Section 3(b) that shows a sample invoice sequence across two months when usage drops below the floor? Our procurement wants concrete numbers in the wording so finance can signoff.

If you can incorporate those three bullets into v4 and return by COB Monday 10/19, we should be able to close on Exhibit C and proceed to signature. If any of those items are blockers, call me and we can triage.
